1	     1	# SMA-567: extend the stream conformance suite
2	     2	
3	     3	Linear: [SMA-567](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-567). Parent design:
4	     4	`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-sma-533-stream-conformance-design.md` (the "SMA-533 design").
5	     5	Suite: `tests/provider-stream-conformance`.
6	     6	
7	     7	## 1. Intent
8	     8	
9	     9	SMA-533 built a cross-provider suite that checks the order of `ModelEvent`s. It scoped itself to
10	    10	its own assertion list and recorded five gaps. This change closes the gaps that captured traffic
11	    11	can support today. It also makes the gaps that captured traffic cannot support yet visible and
12	    12	pinned, so that they cannot disappear in silence.
13	    13	
14	    14	The provenance rule of the suite stays in force without exception. A fixture is transcribed from
15	    15	captured or already-committed captured traffic. It is never written from vendor documentation or
16	    16	from translator code.
17	    17	
18	    18	## 2. Goals, non-goals, anti-goals
19	    19	
20	    20	**Goals.**
21	    21	
22	    22	- G1. Nothing follows an `Err` (ticket item 3).
23	    23	- G2. Reasoning deltas keep the channel order of the wire (ticket item 1).
24	    24	- G3. Parallel tool calls keep their arguments apart (ticket item 2).
25	    25	- G4. Every tool call's arguments parse as JSON, including a zero-argument call (ticket item 4).
26	    26	- G5. The Bedrock `messageStop` / `metadata` wire order is pinned, and `CleanStop` has a
27	    27	  positive-evidence floor for `Usage` (ticket item 3b, changed: see §3.2).
28	    28	- G6. Each (subject, scenario) pair **for a scenario that this change adds** that has no fixture
29	    29	  meeting the provenance rule is a pinned row in a new `UNCAPTURED` table, with a follow-up Linear
30	    30	  issue.
31	    31	
32	    32	**Non-goals.**
33	    33	
34	    34	- No new live captures in this change. Option (A) of the brainstorm was rejected.
35	    35	- No behaviour change to a provider, except a fix for a conformance failure that the suite finds
36	    36	  (SMA-533 design §9 applies without change). Option B (§6.6) keeps Bedrock unchanged.
37	    37	- No new subject.
38	    38	- G3 does not cover arguments of two calls that interleave on the wire (the SMA-550 / SMA-566
39	    39	  bug class). Gemini, the only captured subject, sends each call whole in its own chunk. A capture
40	    40	  with interleaved arguments is input to the parallel follow-up issue.
41	    41	
42	    42	**Anti-goals.** The change fails, even if CI is green, when:
43	    43	
44	    44	- a new fixture has no captured traffic behind it;
45	    45	- a `DECLINED` row says "cannot occur" for a shape that can occur but has no capture;
46	    46	- an `UNCAPTURED` row says "only a capture is missing" when a capture alone cannot let the subject
47	    47	  serve the scenario;
48	    48	- a new rule cannot be shown to fail by a fake or a perturbed sequence;
49	    49	- a subject skips a new scenario without a pinned row.
50	    50	
51	    51	## 3. Facts
52	    52	
53	    53	### 3.1 Captured traffic for each new shape
54	    54	
55	    55	| Shape | Captured, usable | Not captured |
56	    56	| --- | --- | --- |
57	    57	| Reasoning | `anthropic`: `thinking_text_tool_use.txt` (SMA-840 probe run C: thinking, text, `tool_use`) and `empty_thinking_tool_use.txt` (run A: one empty `thinking_delta`, then `tool_use`). | `openai/responses`: `responses_reasoning_then_text.txt` is hand-authored (SMA-316). The gpt-5-mini captures of 2026-11-21 (SMA-585) are not in the repo. `litellm`: inline JSON only. `bedrock`: typed SDK events only. `gemini`: the request never sets `includeThoughts` or `thinkingConfig`, so no thought part arrives on the wire (`providers-gemini/src/lib.rs:59-60`). `openai/chat`: the Chat Completions wire from api.openai.com carries no reasoning text. |
58	    58	| Parallel calls | `gemini`: `parallel_signed.sse`, recorded as "Capture 1" in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-sma-827-gemini-thought-signatures-design.md:299`. | `anthropic`: `parallel_tool_use.txt` came with SMA-317 (commit `d565b58f`) and has no capture behind it. `openai/chat`: `chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt` is hand-authored. `openai/responses`, `litellm`, `bedrock`: inline or typed events only. |
59	    59	| Zero-argument call | `openai/responses`: `responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt`, captured from api.openai.com on 2026-08-22. The API streams **one** `{}` delta, not zero deltas. | All other subjects: hand-written inline tests only. A stream with truly zero argument deltas has no capture for any subject. |
60	    60	| After `Err` | No new fixture. The rule runs on the existing scripts. | — |
61	    61	
62	    62	The spec challenger ran both new captures through the current translators. Both pass every
63	    63	existing assertion and the new rules in §6. Gemini `parallel_signed.sse` gives three calls with
64	    64	native ids, one call-scoped `ProviderData` for each call, and `Finish(ToolCalls)`. The zero-argument
65	    65	capture gives one `{}` delta, `Usage`, and `Finish(ToolCalls)`.
66	    66	
67	    67	### 3.2 The ticket's 3b floor cannot catch the Bedrock swap, so this design does not add it
68	    68	
69	    69	The ticket proposes a floor that requires `Usage` and `Finish` to be adjacent and terminal in
70	    70	`CleanStop`, and says that it "would close" the Bedrock swap. It does not:
71	    71	
72	    72	- When `metadata` comes before `messageStop`, `bedrock/src/stream.rs:253-280` emits `Usage` at
73	    73	  once and `Finish` on the stop. The `ModelEvent` sequence is `…, Usage, Finish` in both orders.
74	    74	- `openai/chat` and `litellm` buffer `Finish` until end-of-stream. A script with the usage chunk
75	    75	  before the `finish_reason` chunk also gives the same events. So the floor cannot see the
76	    76	  SMA-522 fixture mistake either.
77	    77	- All six subjects already pass the floor on their current fixtures. It finds no defect.
78	    78	- The core contract lets `Usage` appear anywhere. On a tool stop, the chat and LiteLLM `finish()`
79	    79	  methods correctly flush a buffered name between `Usage` and `Finish`
80	    80	  (`providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:519-529`, `providers-litellm/src/stream.rs:739-754`).
81	    81	
82	    82	The floor adds a rule that is not in the contract, and no bug class justifies it. This design
83	    83	replaces it with a byte-order check on the Bedrock scripts (§6.5), which does catch the swap, and a
84	    84	positive-evidence floor: `CleanStop` must yield at least one `Usage`.
85	    85	
86	    86	### 3.3 "Nothing after `Err`" conflicts with Bedrock today
87	    87	
88	    88	`Model::invoke` (`core/src/model.rs`) says that `Finish` is terminal and that `Finish` must not
89	    89	follow a mid-stream error. It says nothing about other events after an `Err`.
90	    90	
91	    91	- **Bedrock emits `Usage` after an `Err`.** With `tool_choice: None`, the translator pushes an
92	    92	  `Err` when the model calls a tool (`providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:150-160`). It then emits
93	    93	  `Usage` when `metadata` arrives. The driver yields every item from `consume` and does not stop
94	    94	  after an inner `Err` (`providers-bedrock/src/model.rs:173-177`). The test
95	    95	  `forbid_tool_calls_turns_a_tool_use_into_an_error` (`stream.rs:848-869`) pins `out[1]` as `Usage`.
96	    96	- **Anthropic does not break the rule.** Its driver returns after `consume` returns `Err`
97	    97	  (`providers-anthropic/src/model.rs:145-149`). The `refusal` `Err` (`stream.rs:383`) is produced at
98	    98	  `message_stop`, the last event.
99	    99	- **Gemini, OpenAI and LiteLLM** return after an `Err`. LiteLLM logs and skips an unparseable frame
100	   100	  and emits no `Err`.
101	   101	- No conformance scenario reaches the Bedrock path, so assertion 9 alone stays green.
102	   102	
103	   103	§6.6 holds the decision that this requires.
104	   104	
105	   105	### 3.4 The core accumulator's rule for arguments
106	   106	
107	   107	`ModelTurnAccumulator::build_items` (`core/src/model.rs:640-653`) changes blank or whitespace-only
108	   108	arguments to `{}`, then parses them as any `serde_json::Value`. Arguments that fail to parse make
109	   109	`finish()` return an error. Gemini sends a missing `args` as `"null"` (`providers-gemini/src/sse.rs:45-52`),
110	   110	which parses. Assertion 10 uses the same rule as the accumulator: parse as any JSON value.
111	   111	
112	   112	### 3.5 Existing provenance gaps found on the way
113	   113	
114	   114	For `ToolCallCleanStop`, the `anthropic` subject cites `parallel_tool_use.txt` and the
115	   115	`openai/chat` subject cites `chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt` (`conformance.rs:537-539`, `1649-1653`).
116	   116	Both files are hand-written (§3.1). This change does not fix that. The parallel follow-up issue
117	   117	records it.
118	   118	
119	   119	## 4. Approaches
120	   120	
121	   121	1. **Extend the current machinery (chosen).** Add scenarios, `classify` rules, floors and fakes in
122	   122	   the existing style. Add an `Outcome::Uncaptured` variant and an `UNCAPTURED` table that is
123	   123	   pinned in both directions, the same as `DECLINED`.
124	   124	2. **An opt-in trait for the new scenarios.** Rejected. A subject without a capture would not take
125	   125	   part, so a skip would be invisible again. The pinned-in-both-directions check is the part of
126	   126	   SMA-533 that prevents this.
127	   127	3. **The new checks in each provider crate's tests.** Rejected. The checks would no longer be
128	   128	   cross-provider, which is the purpose of the suite.
129	   129	
130	   130	Sven chose approach 1 and option (C) (a separate `UNCAPTURED` table) on 2026-11-22.
131	   131	
132	   132	## 5. Decisions
133	   133	
134	   134	- D1. `DECLINED` keeps its SMA-533 meaning: the wire shape cannot occur for this subject.
135	   135	- D2. A new pinned table, `UNCAPTURED`, holds the pairs where the shape can occur, a capture alone
136	   136	  would let the subject serve it, and no capture exists. Each row names a follow-up Linear issue.
137	   137	  Only the scenarios that this change adds may have `UNCAPTURED` rows (§6.7).
138	   138	- D3. Bedrock has no wire captures at all. Its existing subject is derived from the SDK types, as
139	   139	  SMA-533 accepted. For the new scenarios, Bedrock takes `UNCAPTURED` rows. New derived fixtures
140	   140	  are not allowed.
141	   141	- D4. Reasoning gets a new provider-neutral scenario, `ReasoningCleanStop`. The existing
142	   142	  `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop` stays the Anthropic signed-thinking scenario, and its `DECLINED` rows
143	   143	  do not change. (The first draft reused `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop`. The challenger showed that
144	   144	  its floors need a call-scoped `ProviderData`, which three of the four subjects never emit, and
145	   145	  that its script leaves out the text block. So the draft's `UNCAPTURED` rows were false.)
146	   146	- D5. Assertion 9 and the floors are rules about fidelity to the wire and the contract. They are
147	   147	  not rules about one provider. Where a rule is stricter than the contract, its doc comment says so.
148	   148	
149	   149	## 6. Design
150	   150	
151	   151	### 6.1 New scenarios
152	   152	
153	   153	| Scenario | Shape | Served by | Declared `FinishReason` |
154	   154	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
155	   155	| `ReasoningCleanStop` | Reasoning, then text, then one tool call, then the stop reason. | `anthropic`, from all of run C (`thinking_text_tool_use.txt`) | `ToolCalls` |
156	   156	| `ParallelToolCallCleanStop` | Two or more complete tool calls, then the stop reason. | `gemini`, from `parallel_signed.sse` | `ToolCalls` |
157	   157	| `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` | One tool call with an empty argument object, then the stop reason. | `openai/responses`, from `responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt` | `ToolCalls` |
158	   158	
159	   159	All three expect a stop reason and end with `Finish`. All three get the clean-stop floor (a
160	   160	`Finish` exists and carries the declared reason). The two tool scenarios get the tool floors.
161	   161	
162	   162	`ReasoningCleanStop` is "clean stop" in the sense of the suite: the stream ends after a stop
163	   163	reason. Its name does not say `end_turn`. The only reasoning capture ends with `tool_use`, so the
164	   164	scenario includes the tool call. The `anthropic` script for it keeps the text block of run C, at
165	   165	index 1, and the `tool_use` at index 2. The text block emits a text-position `ProviderData` with
166	   166	no `call_id` (`providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs:275-279`). Assertion 8 ignores it.
167	   167	
168	   168	Add the three scenarios to `Scenario::ALL`, `expects_stop_reason`, `fakes::conforming`, the
169	   169	`fakes::finish` reason mapping and the `declared_finish_reason` test helper.
170	   170	
171	   171	### 6.2 New `classify` rules
172	   172	
173	   173	These rules need no fixture knowledge, so they go in `classify` and run on every scenario.
174	   174	
175	   175	**Assertion 9: nothing after `Err`** (G1). Any event, `Ok` or `Err`, after the first `Err` is a
176	   176	violation: `Violation::EventAfterError`, with one exception: a `Usage` after an `Err` is allowed
177	   177	(§6.6, option B). Order inside `classify`: after assertion 6 (`FinishAfterError`), so that the
178	   178	more specific name wins for a `Finish` after an `Err`. A positive test shows that `Err, Usage`
179	   179	passes.
180	   180	
181	   181	**Assertion 10: tool arguments parse as JSON** (G4). Runs only when the stream contains a
182	   182	`Finish`. A truncated, errored or cancelled stream can correctly end in the middle of the
183	   183	arguments, and a consumer calls `finish()` only after a `Finish`. For each `call_id` group,
184	   184	concatenate the `args_delta`s in stream order. Blank or whitespace-only becomes `{}`. The result
185	   185	must parse as a JSON value: `Violation::ToolArgsNotJson { call_id }`. This is the accumulator's
186	   186	rule (§3.4). A blank-`call_id` group is checked only when it carries exactly one name. With two
187	   187	or more names, the group holds several calls, and the accumulator refuses that turn anyway
188	   188	(SMA-621). Assertion 10 runs on every tool scenario for every subject, so it also covers the
189	   189	existing fixtures. All existing served fixtures pass it today.
190	   190	
191	   191	### 6.3 New floor checks
192	   192	
193	   193	These checks need fixture knowledge, so they go in `floor_violation`, the same as the existing
194	   194	`FinishReasonMismatch` check. The existing rule of `floor_violation` stays: a floor reports only
195	   195	missing evidence, or a mismatch with a declaration. It leaves the exact diagnosis to `classify`.
196	   196	
197	   197	**No `Err` outside the error scenarios.** In every scenario except `ErrorMidGeneration` and
198	   198	`ErrorAfterStopReason`, the stream must yield no `Err`. Today, nothing stops a clean script from
199	   199	being read as an error. This floor closes the SMA-533 §6 statement that S3 "will not be
200	   200	mis-reported as S4a".
201	   201	
202	   202	**`CleanStop` yields a `Usage`.** Every `CleanStop` script carries usage, so a stream without
203	   203	`Usage` did not serve the scenario's bytes.
204	   204	
205	   205	**Channel order** (G2). A new trait method declares the run order of the fixture for a scenario:
206	   206	
207	   207	```rust
208	   208	/// One run of same-channel events, in wire order.
209	   209	pub enum Channel { Reasoning, Text, Tool }
210	   210	
211	   211	fn fixture_channel_order(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<&'static [Channel]>;
212	   212	```
213	   213	
214	   214	`None` means "no claim". For `ReasoningCleanStop`, the subject must return `Some(..)`. If it
215	   215	returns `None`, the floor fails with `InsufficientEvidence`. The check maps each `ReasoningDelta`,
216	   216	`TokenDelta` and `ToolCallDelta` to its channel, ignores all other events, merges adjacent equal
217	   217	channels into one run, and compares the result with the declared order:
218	   218	`Violation::ChannelOrderMismatch { expected, observed }`. A further floor for `ReasoningCleanStop`
219	   219	requires at least one `ReasoningDelta`.
220	   220	
221	   221	The contract lets the three channels interleave freely (`core/src/model.rs:56-57`). This check is
222	   222	therefore about fidelity to the wire order, not about the contract. Its doc comment says so. An
223	   223	empty delta still counts as a run. Run A shows that a real wire can carry an empty
224	   224	`thinking_delta`, and the translator passes it on as an empty `ReasoningDelta`.
225	   225	
226	   226	The `anthropic` declaration for `ReasoningCleanStop` is `[Reasoning, Text, Tool]`, read from run C.
227	   227	
228	   228	**Declared calls** (G3, G4). A new trait method declares the calls in the fixture:
229	   229	
230	   230	```rust
231	   231	/// A tool call the fixture carries: its name and its complete arguments as JSON text.
232	   232	pub struct ExpectedCall { pub name: &'static str, pub args: &'static str }
233	   233	
234	   234	fn fixture_calls(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> &'static [ExpectedCall];
235	   235	```
236	   236	
237	   237	`args` is a `&'static str` so that the table can be a `const`. The floor parses it.
238	   238	`fixture_calls` must return a non-empty list for `ParallelToolCallCleanStop` and
239	   239	`ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop`, and an empty list for every other scenario. The existing tool
240	   240	scenarios keep `fixture_tool_name`, which does not change. For the two new scenarios, the
241	   241	"declared name is present" floor reads the names from `fixture_calls`. So the Gemini names
242	   242	(`search`, `weather`) and the zero-argument name (`get_current_time`) need no change to
243	   243	`fixture_tool_name`.
244	   244	
245	   245	For both new scenarios:
246	   246	
247	   247	- the observed calls, in first-seen `call_id` order, must equal the declared calls by name and by
248	   248	  parsed arguments: `Violation::ToolCallsMismatch { expected, observed }`;
249	   249	- a call whose arguments do not parse is skipped by this floor, so that assertion 10 reports it
250	   250	  with its exact name;
251	   251	- the match is by position, not by `call_id`, because a subject cannot always declare the ids
252	   252	  that its translator makes.
253	   253	
254	   254	For `ParallelToolCallCleanStop`, a further floor requires two or more distinct non-blank
255	   255	`call_id`s. For `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop`, the declared call is `get_current_time` with arguments
256	   256	`{}`. So a fixture with real arguments fails the floor, and the scenario cannot pass vacuously.
257	   257	
258	   258	### 6.4 `Outcome::Uncaptured` and the `UNCAPTURED` table
259	   259	
260	   260	```rust
261	   261	pub enum Outcome {
262	   262	    Served { .. },
263	   263	    Declined(&'static str),
264	   264	    /// The wire shape can occur for this provider, and a capture alone would let the subject
265	   265	    /// serve it, but no fixture that meets the provenance rule exists. The reason must match the
266	   266	    /// pinned `UNCAPTURED` table.
267	   267	    Uncaptured(&'static str),
268	   268	}
269	   269	
270	   270	/// (subject, scenario, reason, follow-up Linear issue)
271	   271	pub const UNCAPTURED: &[(&str, Scenario, &str, &str)] = &[ .. ];
272	   272	```
273	   273	
274	   274	An `Uncaptured` outcome is not served. No floor or assertion runs for it, the same as `Declined`.
275	   275	
276	   276	`assert_conforms` collects uncaptured pairs separately from declined pairs and checks them against
277	   277	`UNCAPTURED` in both directions, the same as `assert_declines_match`: an unpinned pair, a stale row
278	   278	and a changed reason each fail. The two outcomes are not interchangeable. A subject that reports
279	   279	`Uncaptured` for a pair that `DECLINED` lists fails, and the reverse also fails.
280	   280	
281	   281	Static unit tests in `declines.rs`:
282	   282	
283	   283	1. No pair appears in both tables.
284	   284	2. Every subject in `UNCAPTURED` is in `REGISTERED_SUBJECTS` (extend
285	   285	   `every_declined_subject_is_registered`).
286	   286	3. Every follow-up field matches `^SMA-\d+$`.
287	   287	4. For each scenario in `Scenario::ALL`, at least one registered subject is in neither table. So
288	   288	   no scenario can end up served by nobody.
289	   289	5. `UNCAPTURED` rows name only scenarios from an explicit allow-list, which holds the three new
290	   290	   scenarios. Moving an SMA-533 scenario into `UNCAPTURED` then needs a reviewed edit to that list.
291	   291	
292	   292	Each follow-up issue states in its acceptance criteria that the issue closes only when its rows
293	   293	are removed: by a capture, or by a reviewed move to `DECLINED`.
294	   294	
295	   295	### 6.5 The Bedrock wire-order check
296	   296	
297	   297	This is G5. Add a function in the `bedrock` module of `tests/conformance.rs` that takes a chunk
298	   298	list and fails when a `metadata` frame comes before a `messageStop` frame. It finds each frame by
299	   299	its `:event-type` header. If `src/eventstream.rs` has no header reader, add a minimal one in the
300	   300	test code. It must decode the header block, not copy the encoder.
301	   301	
302	   302	- Run the function on every Bedrock script that has both frames (`CleanStop`, `ToolCallCleanStop`
303	   303	  and any other).
304	   304	- Unit-test the function on a swapped list, so that the proof that it can fail stays in the code.
305	   305	- Replace the "do not reorder it casually" prose in the `metadata()` doc (`conformance.rs`,
306	   306	  near lines 168-181) with a pointer to the check. Keep the reason in the prose.
307	   307	
308	   308	### 6.6 The contract for events after an `Err` (decided: option B)
309	   309	
310	   310	Sven chose option B on 2026-11-22. The reason: the tokens were consumed, so the `Usage` is real
311	   311	billing data. The options were:
312	   312	
313	   313	- **A. An `Err` is terminal without exception.** Add to the `Model::invoke` ordering list, after
314	   314	  "`Finish` is the terminal event; nothing follows it.":
315	   315	
316	   316	  > - An `Err` item is terminal too: implementations MUST NOT yield any item after it.
317	   317	
318	   318	  The Bedrock driver then stops after it yields an inner `Err`. The `Usage` that comes after the
319	   319	  `tool_choice: None` error is lost, and `forbid_tool_calls_turns_a_tool_use_into_an_error`
320	   320	  changes. Assertion 9 is strict.
321	   321	- **B. An `Err` is terminal, except for a trailing `Usage`.** The sentence allows `Usage` events
322	   322	  after an `Err` and nothing else. Assertion 9 exempts `Usage`. Bedrock does not change.
323	   323	  **Chosen.** The sentence to add to the `Model::invoke` ordering list is:
324	   324	
325	   325	  > - An `Err` item is terminal for every event except `Usage`: implementations MUST NOT yield
326	   326	  >   any item after an `Err` other than `Usage` snapshots for the same response.
327	   327	
328	   328	In both cases, add a translator-level test in `providers-bedrock`, because no conformance scenario
329	   329	reaches this path.
330	   330	
331	   331	The contract sentence is a doc-only change to `paigasus-helikon-core`. It goes in its own commit,
332	   332	`docs(core): SMA-567 …`. No `version` field is edited by hand. release-plz then gives `core` a
333	   333	patch bump and the dependants get the facade cascade. The PR body says this. The CHANGELOG entry

1	# SMA-567: extend the stream conformance suite
     2	
     3	Linear: [SMA-567](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-567). Parent design:
     4	`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-19-sma-533-stream-conformance-design.md` (the "SMA-533 design").
     5	Suite: `tests/provider-stream-conformance`.
     6	
     7	## 1. Intent
     8	
     9	SMA-533 built a cross-provider suite that checks the order of `ModelEvent`s. It scoped itself to
    10	its own assertion list and recorded five gaps. This change closes the gaps that captured traffic
    11	can support today. It also makes the gaps that captured traffic cannot support yet visible and
    12	pinned, so that they cannot disappear in silence.
    13	
    14	The provenance rule of the suite stays in force without exception. A fixture is transcribed from
    15	captured or already-committed captured traffic. It is never written from vendor documentation or
    16	from translator code.
    17	
    18	## 2. Goals, non-goals, anti-goals
    19	
    20	**Goals.**
    21	
    22	- G1. Nothing follows an `Err` (ticket item 3).
    23	- G2. Reasoning deltas keep the channel order of the wire (ticket item 1).
    24	- G3. Parallel tool calls keep their arguments apart (ticket item 2).
    25	- G4. Every tool call's arguments parse as JSON, including a zero-argument call (ticket item 4).
    26	- G5. The Bedrock `messageStop` / `metadata` wire order is pinned, and `CleanStop` has a
    27	  positive-evidence floor for `Usage` (ticket item 3b, changed: see §3.2).
    28	- G6. Each (subject, scenario) pair **for a scenario that this change adds** that has no fixture
    29	  meeting the provenance rule is a pinned row in a new `UNCAPTURED` table, with a follow-up Linear
    30	  issue.
    31	
    32	**Non-goals.**
    33	
    34	- No new live captures in this change. Option (A) of the brainstorm was rejected.
    35	- No behaviour change to a provider, except a fix for a conformance failure that the suite finds
    36	  (SMA-533 design §9 applies without change). Option B (§6.6) keeps Bedrock unchanged.
    37	- No new subject.
    38	- G3 does not cover arguments of two calls that interleave on the wire (the SMA-550 / SMA-566
    39	  bug class). Gemini, the only captured subject, sends each call whole in its own chunk. A capture
    40	  with interleaved arguments is input to the parallel follow-up issue.
    41	
    42	**Anti-goals.** The change fails, even if CI is green, when:
    43	
    44	- a new fixture has no captured traffic behind it;
    45	- a `DECLINED` row says "cannot occur" for a shape that can occur but has no capture;
    46	- an `UNCAPTURED` row says "only a capture is missing" when a capture alone cannot let the subject
    47	  serve the scenario;
    48	- a new rule cannot be shown to fail by a fake or a perturbed sequence;
    49	- a subject skips a new scenario without a pinned row.
    50	
    51	## 3. Facts
    52	
    53	### 3.1 Captured traffic for each new shape
    54	
    55	| Shape | Captured, usable | Not captured |
    56	| --- | --- | --- |
    57	| Reasoning | `anthropic`: `thinking_text_tool_use.txt` (SMA-840 probe run C: thinking, text, `tool_use`) and `empty_thinking_tool_use.txt` (run A: one empty `thinking_delta`, then `tool_use`). | `openai/responses`: `responses_reasoning_then_text.txt` is hand-authored (SMA-316). The gpt-5-mini captures of 2026-11-21 (SMA-585) are not in the repo. `litellm`: inline JSON only. `bedrock`: typed SDK events only. `gemini`: the request never sets `includeThoughts` or `thinkingConfig`, so no thought part arrives on the wire (`providers-gemini/src/lib.rs:59-60`). `openai/chat`: the Chat Completions wire from api.openai.com carries no reasoning text. |
    58	| Parallel calls | `gemini`: `parallel_signed.sse`, recorded as "Capture 1" in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-sma-827-gemini-thought-signatures-design.md:299`. | `anthropic`: `parallel_tool_use.txt` came with SMA-317 (commit `d565b58f`) and has no capture behind it. `openai/chat`: `chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt` is hand-authored. `openai/responses`, `litellm`, `bedrock`: inline or typed events only. |
    59	| Zero-argument call | `openai/responses`: `responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt`, captured from api.openai.com on 2026-08-22. The API streams **one** `{}` delta, not zero deltas. | All other subjects: hand-written inline tests only. A stream with truly zero argument deltas has no capture for any subject. |
    60	| After `Err` | No new fixture. The rule runs on the existing scripts. | — |
    61	
    62	The spec challenger ran both new captures through the current translators. Both pass every
    63	existing assertion and the new rules in §6. Gemini `parallel_signed.sse` gives three calls with
    64	native ids, one call-scoped `ProviderData` for each call, and `Finish(ToolCalls)`. The zero-argument
    65	capture gives one `{}` delta, `Usage`, and `Finish(ToolCalls)`.
    66	
    67	### 3.2 The ticket's 3b floor cannot catch the Bedrock swap, so this design does not add it
    68	
    69	The ticket proposes a floor that requires `Usage` and `Finish` to be adjacent and terminal in
    70	`CleanStop`, and says that it "would close" the Bedrock swap. It does not:
    71	
    72	- When `metadata` comes before `messageStop`, `bedrock/src/stream.rs:253-280` emits `Usage` at
    73	  once and `Finish` on the stop. The `ModelEvent` sequence is `…, Usage, Finish` in both orders.
    74	- `openai/chat` and `litellm` buffer `Finish` until end-of-stream. A script with the usage chunk
    75	  before the `finish_reason` chunk also gives the same events. So the floor cannot see the
    76	  SMA-522 fixture mistake either.
    77	- All six subjects already pass the floor on their current fixtures. It finds no defect.
    78	- The core contract lets `Usage` appear anywhere. On a tool stop, the chat and LiteLLM `finish()`
    79	  methods correctly flush a buffered name between `Usage` and `Finish`
    80	  (`providers-openai/src/backend/chat.rs:519-529`, `providers-litellm/src/stream.rs:739-754`).
    81	
    82	The floor adds a rule that is not in the contract, and no bug class justifies it. This design
    83	replaces it with a byte-order check on the Bedrock scripts (§6.5), which does catch the swap, and a
    84	positive-evidence floor: `CleanStop` must yield at least one `Usage`.
    85	
    86	### 3.3 "Nothing after `Err`" conflicts with Bedrock today
    87	
    88	`Model::invoke` (`core/src/model.rs`) says that `Finish` is terminal and that `Finish` must not
    89	follow a mid-stream error. It says nothing about other events after an `Err`.
    90	
    91	- **Bedrock emits `Usage` after an `Err`.** With `tool_choice: None`, the translator pushes an
    92	  `Err` when the model calls a tool (`providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs:150-160`). It then emits
    93	  `Usage` when `metadata` arrives. The driver yields every item from `consume` and does not stop
    94	  after an inner `Err` (`providers-bedrock/src/model.rs:173-177`). The test
    95	  `forbid_tool_calls_turns_a_tool_use_into_an_error` (`stream.rs:848-869`) pins `out[1]` as `Usage`.
    96	- **Anthropic does not break the rule.** Its driver returns after `consume` returns `Err`
    97	  (`providers-anthropic/src/model.rs:145-149`). The `refusal` `Err` (`stream.rs:383`) is produced at
    98	  `message_stop`, the last event.
    99	- **Gemini, OpenAI and LiteLLM** return after an `Err`. LiteLLM logs and skips an unparseable frame
   100	  and emits no `Err`.
   101	- No conformance scenario reaches the Bedrock path, so assertion 9 alone stays green.
   102	
   103	§6.6 holds the decision that this requires.
   104	
   105	### 3.4 The core accumulator's rule for arguments
   106	
   107	`ModelTurnAccumulator::build_items` (`core/src/model.rs:640-653`) changes blank or whitespace-only
   108	arguments to `{}`, then parses them as any `serde_json::Value`. Arguments that fail to parse make
   109	`finish()` return an error. Gemini sends a missing `args` as `"null"` (`providers-gemini/src/sse.rs:45-52`),
   110	which parses. Assertion 10 uses the same rule as the accumulator: parse as any JSON value.
   111	
   112	### 3.5 Existing provenance gaps found on the way
   113	
   114	For `ToolCallCleanStop`, the `anthropic` subject cites `parallel_tool_use.txt` and the
   115	`openai/chat` subject cites `chat_parallel_tool_calls.txt` (`conformance.rs:537-539`, `1649-1653`).
   116	Both files are hand-written (§3.1). This change does not fix that. The parallel follow-up issue
   117	records it.
   118	
   119	## 4. Approaches
   120	
   121	1. **Extend the current machinery (chosen).** Add scenarios, `classify` rules, floors and fakes in
   122	   the existing style. Add an `Outcome::Uncaptured` variant and an `UNCAPTURED` table that is
   123	   pinned in both directions, the same as `DECLINED`.
   124	2. **An opt-in trait for the new scenarios.** Rejected. A subject without a capture would not take
   125	   part, so a skip would be invisible again. The pinned-in-both-directions check is the part of
   126	   SMA-533 that prevents this.
   127	3. **The new checks in each provider crate's tests.** Rejected. The checks would no longer be
   128	   cross-provider, which is the purpose of the suite.
   129	
   130	Sven chose approach 1 and option (C) (a separate `UNCAPTURED` table) on 2026-11-22.
   131	
   132	## 5. Decisions
   133	
   134	- D1. `DECLINED` keeps its SMA-533 meaning: the wire shape cannot occur for this subject.
   135	- D2. A new pinned table, `UNCAPTURED`, holds the pairs where the shape can occur, a capture alone
   136	  would let the subject serve it, and no capture exists. Each row names a follow-up Linear issue.
   137	  Only the scenarios that this change adds may have `UNCAPTURED` rows (§6.7).
   138	- D3. Bedrock has no wire captures at all. Its existing subject is derived from the SDK types, as
   139	  SMA-533 accepted. For the new scenarios, Bedrock takes `UNCAPTURED` rows. New derived fixtures
   140	  are not allowed.
   141	- D4. Reasoning gets a new provider-neutral scenario, `ReasoningCleanStop`. The existing
   142	  `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop` stays the Anthropic signed-thinking scenario, and its `DECLINED` rows
   143	  do not change. (The first draft reused `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop`. The challenger showed that
   144	  its floors need a call-scoped `ProviderData`, which three of the four subjects never emit, and
   145	  that its script leaves out the text block. So the draft's `UNCAPTURED` rows were false.)
   146	- D5. Assertion 9 and the floors are rules about fidelity to the wire and the contract. They are
   147	  not rules about one provider. Where a rule is stricter than the contract, its doc comment says so.
   148	
   149	## 6. Design
   150	
   151	### 6.1 New scenarios
   152	
   153	| Scenario | Shape | Served by | Declared `FinishReason` |
   154	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
   155	| `ReasoningCleanStop` | Reasoning, then text, then one tool call, then the stop reason. | `anthropic`, from all of run C (`thinking_text_tool_use.txt`) | `ToolCalls` |
   156	| `ParallelToolCallCleanStop` | Two or more complete tool calls, then the stop reason. | `gemini`, from `parallel_signed.sse` | `ToolCalls` |
   157	| `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` | One tool call with an empty argument object, then the stop reason. | `openai/responses`, from `responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt` | `ToolCalls` |
   158	
   159	All three expect a stop reason and end with `Finish`. All three get the clean-stop floor (a
   160	`Finish` exists and carries the declared reason). The two tool scenarios get the tool floors.
   161	
   162	`ReasoningCleanStop` is "clean stop" in the sense of the suite: the stream ends after a stop
   163	reason. Its name does not say `end_turn`. The only reasoning capture ends with `tool_use`, so the
   164	scenario includes the tool call. The `anthropic` script for it keeps the text block of run C, at
   165	index 1, and the `tool_use` at index 2. The text block emits a text-position `ProviderData` with
   166	no `call_id` (`providers-anthropic/src/stream.rs:275-279`). Assertion 8 ignores it.
   167	
   168	Add the three scenarios to `Scenario::ALL`, `expects_stop_reason`, `fakes::conforming`, the
   169	`fakes::finish` reason mapping and the `declared_finish_reason` test helper.
   170	
   171	### 6.2 New `classify` rules
   172	
   173	These rules need no fixture knowledge, so they go in `classify` and run on every scenario.
   174	
   175	**Assertion 9: nothing after `Err`** (G1). Any event, `Ok` or `Err`, after the first `Err` is a
   176	violation: `Violation::EventAfterError`, with one exception: a `Usage` after an `Err` is allowed
   177	(§6.6, option B). Order inside `classify`: after assertion 6 (`FinishAfterError`), so that the
   178	more specific name wins for a `Finish` after an `Err`. A positive test shows that `Err, Usage`
   179	passes.
   180	
   181	**Assertion 10: tool arguments parse as JSON** (G4). Runs only when the stream contains a
   182	`Finish`. A truncated, errored or cancelled stream can correctly end in the middle of the
   183	arguments, and a consumer calls `finish()` only after a `Finish`. For each `call_id` group,
   184	concatenate the `args_delta`s in stream order. Blank or whitespace-only becomes `{}`. The result
   185	must parse as a JSON value: `Violation::ToolArgsNotJson { call_id }`. This is the accumulator's
   186	rule (§3.4). A blank-`call_id` group is checked only when it carries exactly one name. With two
   187	or more names, the group holds several calls, and the accumulator refuses that turn anyway
   188	(SMA-621). Assertion 10 runs on every tool scenario for every subject, so it also covers the
   189	existing fixtures. All existing served fixtures pass it today.
   190	
   191	### 6.3 New floor checks
   192	
   193	These checks need fixture knowledge, so they go in `floor_violation`, the same as the existing
   194	`FinishReasonMismatch` check. The existing rule of `floor_violation` stays: a floor reports only
   195	missing evidence, or a mismatch with a declaration. It leaves the exact diagnosis to `classify`.
   196	
   197	**No `Err` outside the error scenarios.** In every scenario except `ErrorMidGeneration` and
   198	`ErrorAfterStopReason`, the stream must yield no `Err`. Today, nothing stops a clean script from
   199	being read as an error. This floor closes the SMA-533 §6 statement that S3 "will not be
   200	mis-reported as S4a".
   201	
   202	**`CleanStop` yields a `Usage`.** Every `CleanStop` script carries usage, so a stream without
   203	`Usage` did not serve the scenario's bytes.
   204	
   205	**Channel order** (G2). A new trait method declares the run order of the fixture for a scenario:
   206	
   207	```rust
   208	/// One run of same-channel events, in wire order.
   209	pub enum Channel { Reasoning, Text, Tool }
   210	
   211	fn fixture_channel_order(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<&'static [Channel]>;
   212	```
   213	
   214	`None` means "no claim". For `ReasoningCleanStop`, the subject must return `Some(..)`. If it
   215	returns `None`, the floor fails with `InsufficientEvidence`. The check maps each `ReasoningDelta`,
   216	`TokenDelta` and `ToolCallDelta` to its channel, ignores all other events, merges adjacent equal
   217	channels into one run, and compares the result with the declared order:
   218	`Violation::ChannelOrderMismatch { expected, observed }`. A further floor for `ReasoningCleanStop`
   219	requires at least one `ReasoningDelta`.
   220	
   221	The contract lets the three channels interleave freely (`core/src/model.rs:56-57`). This check is
   222	therefore about fidelity to the wire order, not about the contract. Its doc comment says so. An
   223	empty delta still counts as a run. Run A shows that a real wire can carry an empty

   199	const UNCAPTURED_SCENARIOS: &[Scenario] = &[

   205	/// The subject names registered in `tests/conformance.rs` — one `mod` per
   206	/// subject, each holding a `StreamUnderTest` impl whose `name()` returns one
   207	/// of these strings.
   208	///
   209	/// [`DECLINED`] is checked against this list because a typo'd subject name in
   210	/// the table would otherwise be silently invisible: `assert_declines_match`
   211	/// only ever runs with a real subject's name, filtering [`DECLINED`] down to
   212	/// the rows for that one subject. A row naming a subject that does not exist
   213	/// never matches that filter for *any* real subject, so it is never checked
   214	/// in either direction — not flagged as an unexpected decline, and not
   215	/// flagged as a pinned decline that stopped happening. The reverse direction
   216	/// (a real subject declining something absent from the table) does fail
   217	/// loudly; this is the direction that previously did not.
   218	#[cfg(test)]
   219	const REGISTERED_SUBJECTS: &[&str] = &[
   220	    "anthropic",
   221	    "gemini",
   222	    "bedrock",
   223	    "litellm",
   224	    "openai/chat",
   225	    "openai/responses",
   226	];

   228	#[cfg(test)]
   229	mod tests {
   230	    use super::*;
   231	
   232	    /// Every subject named in [`DECLINED`] must be one this suite actually
   233	    /// registers. Misspell one (e.g. `"bedrok"`) and this fails; the row
   234	    /// would otherwise sit in the table forever, never compared against any
   235	    /// real subject's observed declines.
   236	    #[test]
   237	    fn every_declined_subject_is_registered() {
   238	        for (subject, scenario, reason) in DECLINED {
   239	            assert!(
   240	                REGISTERED_SUBJECTS.contains(subject),
   241	                "DECLINED names {subject:?} for {scenario:?} ({reason:?}), which is not a \
   242	                 registered subject name ({REGISTERED_SUBJECTS:?}) — check for a typo"
   243	            );
   244	        }
   245	    }
   246	
   247	    /// No pair is both declined and uncaptured.
   248	    #[test]
   249	    fn no_pair_is_in_both_tables() {
   250	        for (subject, scenario, _) in DECLINED {
   251	            assert!(
   252	                !UNCAPTURED
   253	                    .iter()
   254	                    .any(|(s, sc, _, _)| s == subject && sc == scenario),
   255	                "{subject:?} / {scenario:?} is in both DECLINED and UNCAPTURED"
   256	            );
   257	        }
   258	    }
   259

   261	    #[test]
   262	    fn every_uncaptured_subject_is_registered() {
   263	        for (subject, scenario, reason, _) in UNCAPTURED {
   264	            assert!(
   265	                REGISTERED_SUBJECTS.contains(subject),
   266	                "UNCAPTURED names {subject:?} for {scenario:?} ({reason:?}), which is not a \
   267	                 registered subject name ({REGISTERED_SUBJECTS:?})"
   268	            );
   269	        }
   270	    }
   271	
   272	    /// Each follow-up field is a Linear id, `SMA-` and digits.
   273	    #[test]
   274	    fn every_follow_up_is_a_linear_id() {
   275	        for (subject, scenario, _, follow_up) in UNCAPTURED {
   276	            let ok = follow_up
   277	                .strip_prefix("SMA-")
   278	                .is_some_and(|d| !d.is_empty() && d.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()));
   279	            assert!(
   280	                ok,
   281	                "{subject:?} / {scenario:?}: follow-up {follow_up:?} is not SMA-<digits>"
   282	            );
   283	        }
   284	    }
   285	
   286	    /// No scenario may end up served by nobody.
   287	    #[test]
   288	    fn every_scenario_has_a_serving_subject() {
   289	        for scenario in Scenario::ALL {
   290	            let served = REGISTERED_SUBJECTS.iter().any(|name| {
   291	                !DECLINED
   292	                    .iter()
   293	                    .any(|(s, sc, _)| s == name && sc == scenario)
   294	                    && !UNCAPTURED
   295	                        .iter()
   296	                        .any(|(s, sc, _, _)| s == name && sc == scenario)
   297	            });
   298	            assert!(served, "{scenario:?} has no subject that serves it");
   299	        }
   300	    }
   301	
   302	    /// `UNCAPTURED` names only scenarios from the explicit allow-list.
   303	    #[test]
   304	    fn uncaptured_rows_name_only_allow_listed_scenarios() {
   305	        for (subject, scenario, _, _) in UNCAPTURED {
   306	            assert!(
   307	                UNCAPTURED_SCENARIOS.contains(scenario),
   308	                "UNCAPTURED names {scenario:?} for {subject:?}, which is not in \
   309	                 UNCAPTURED_SCENARIOS"
   310	            );
   311	        }
   312	    }
   313	}

## Final whole-branch review: SMA-567 (076a332f..7a1615b8)

I read the spec, the plan, the ledger (R1 to R4 and the parked items) and the full diff, in passes: core/book/bedrock, `lib.rs`, `check.rs`, `fakes.rs`, `declines.rs`, then `conformance.rs`. I did not run cargo, because the CI-gate run is in progress. I checked the three new fixtures against their source files with a script that does not build anything:
- The Gemini `PARALLEL_SIGNED` frames are byte-identical to `parallel_signed.sse` (1799 = 1799 bytes).
- All five `ZERO_ARG_EVENTS` `event:`/`data:` pairs occur verbatim in `responses_tool_call_zero_args.txt`.
- I compared the run C script line by line with `thinking_text_tool_use.txt`. The texts are the same: 15 thinking deltas, 12 text deltas and 4 argument fragments, plus the `message_start` and `message_delta` keys and values, the `caller` key, the ids and `SIG_FAKE_1`.

### Strengths

- **§9 coverage is complete.**
  - The spec asks for eight perturbed floor tests. All of them exist (`lib.rs:1866-2170`).
  - The three `classify` fakes are in `every_fake_is_rejected_with_its_classification`. Positive tests cover `Err, Usage`, blank arguments, whitespace-only arguments, `null` arguments, a truncated stream, and a blank id with one name and with two names.
  - The three `UNCAPTURED` negative tests exist. The reverse-direction test that the ledger carried forward also exists: `a_declined_outcome_for_an_uncaptured_pair_fails`.
  - All five static tests from §6.4 are in `declines.rs:236-312`.
- **All 18 new (subject, scenario) pairs are covered.** Each one is served, declined or uncaptured. The reasons in `conformance.rs` and in the mock `Subject` match `DECLINED` and `UNCAPTURED` exactly.
- **The provenance comments match the scripts.** The edit lists are accurate: run C has edits 1-3, and Gemini and the zero-argument script have "no payload edits". Each comment cites the correct source and capture.
- **The Bedrock check is good.** It decodes frames with the SDK decoder, so it does not copy the encoder. It asserts that `CleanStop` and `ToolCallCleanStop` are both checked, and it has a swapped-order `should_panic` test.
- **Option B is the same in all four places:** the core sentence, the book, the `classify` exemption, and the translator test that pins `[Err, Usage]` and nothing from `finish()`.
- **The pinned check reports both directions at once** (R1, `lib.rs:489-511`). This gives a better diagnosis than the old single-table assert.
- **The new trait methods use exhaustive `match` arms.** The ledger carried this item forward, and it is done.

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)

None.

#### Important (Should Fix)

1. **The `floor_violation` doc is now false, and the Err-count floor hides a diagnosis that `classify` now gives.**
   - File: `tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/lib.rs:652-653` (doc) and `:957-967` (floor).
   - What is wrong: the doc says the Err count is the one exception "because `classify` has no rule for a stream that errors twice". Assertion 9 (Task 2) is now that rule. `[Err, Err]` and `[Err, Usage, Err]` classify as `EventAfterError` (`check.rs:59-74`; the comment at `check.rs:65` says so). The floors run before `classify`, so the "more than one Err" half of the floor reports `InsufficientEvidence` first. The doc's own principle (`lib.rs:643-650`) says a floor that rejects excess "would mask … behind `InsufficientEvidence`, which is the wrong diagnosis".
   - Why it matters: spec §6.10 puts the `floor_violation` doc on the must-update list. The ledger parked this item as "may read stale", but the sentence is false, not only stale.
   - Fix: make the floor check `== 0` only, and change its message. Then delete the "one exception" paragraph or rewrite it to point to assertion 9. If you want to keep the floor, rewrite the paragraph to say that assertion 9 also catches the excess and that the floor keeps it as a wire-fidelity check.

2. **No test shows that the "declares no calls" floor fails for `ReasoningCleanStop`.**
   - File: `lib.rs:755-766`.
   - What is wrong: R2 added `ReasoningCleanStop` to this floor. Negative tests exist only for `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop` (`:2091`) and `ParallelToolCallCleanStop` (`:2134`). A mutation that removes `Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop` from the `matches!` at `:757` passes every test.
   - Why it matters: spec §2 has the anti-goal "a new rule cannot be shown to fail".
   - Fix: add `a_reasoning_scenario_without_declared_calls_fails`. Call `floor_violation(ReasoningCleanStop, conforming(..), TOOL_NAME, Some(ToolCalls), Some(REASONING_ORDER), &[])` and expect "declares no calls".

#### Minor (Nice to Have)

1. **`[Err, Err]` has no `classify` test** (parked after T2). The comment at `check.rs:65-66` says that a later `Err` is a violation, but no test pins it. Add one test (`[token, Err, Err]` gives `EventAfterError`). This is also the evidence that makes Important item 1 safe to fix.
2. **Stale doc references made by this change:**
   - `declines.rs:1`: "The pinned decline set." The file now holds two tables.
   - `declines.rs:210`: names `assert_declines_match`, which is gone. It is now `pinned_problems`. Also, `UNCAPTURED` is checked against `REGISTERED_SUBJECTS` too.
   - `fakes.rs:10`: "the decline cross-check". Change it to "the decline and uncaptured cross-checks".
   - `fakes.rs:24`: "every tool-bearing fake uses" `c1`. The parallel fake also uses `c2`.
   - `conformance.rs:197`, `:897-898`, `:1466-1467`, `:2310-2311`, `:3118-3119`, `:3840-3841`: the `script` docs say `None` only for declined scenarios. `script` now also returns `None` for uncaptured ones.
   - `conformance.rs:2079-2080`: the `thinking_delta` doc says "the text itself is arbitrary". The run C script now sends captured text.
3. **Line-wrap gaps** (parked after T7, still present): `lib.rs:311-313` (the `fixture_calls` doc), `lib.rs:678-679` (the floor doc), and `conformance.rs:22-24` (header rule 1, "cross-check by construction," is on a short line).
4. **The panic message cites two specs without saying which.** `lib.rs:509` says "(spec §6.2, §6.4)". §6.2 is in the SMA-533 design and §6.4 is in the SMA-567 design. Name both.
5. **The zero-argument floor test passes the wrong tool name** (parked after T7). `lib.rs:2074` passes `TOOL_NAME`, not `ZERO_ARG_TOOL_NAME`. This has no effect, because a non-empty `calls` list replaces `tool_name`. For consistency, change it to the `:2097` form.
6. **The no-`Err` floor (`lib.rs:928-942`) is stricter than the contract for the truncation scenarios, and its comment does not say so.** The contract does not forbid a translator from turning a truncated body into an `Err`. D5 says a rule stricter than the contract must say so in its doc. The message "did not serve the bytes the scenario describes" would mislead the person who reads a failure caused by such a translator. Add one sentence that says this is a fidelity floor on the scripts, not a contract rule.
7. **Book paragraph order.** At `docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md:66-69`, the new sentence comes after "Both rules restate `Model::invoke`'s existing public contract". The new rule is a third rule and it is not "existing". Move it above that sentence, or change the wording to "These rules restate…".
8. **The run C prompt does not match the capture** (parked after T5). In `conformance.rs:2524-2527`, the `request()` prompt asks about Berlin, but run C is about Paris. This has no effect on the wire. It is optional to fix.
9. **The crate-level doc at `lib.rs:10` points only to the SMA-533 design.** Add the SMA-567 design as the record for assertions 9 and 10, the new floors and `UNCAPTURED`.

### Triage of the parked ledger items

| Parked item | Ruling |
| --- | --- |
| T2: no `[Err, Err]` test | Fix before merge (Minor 1). Fix it together with Important 1. |
| T2: floors run before `classify` | This is the cause of Important 1. Fix it. |
| T4: "the one exception is the Err count" doc | Fix before merge (Important 1). It is false, not only stale. |
| T5: Berlin/Paris prompt | Optional. |
| T7: line-wrap gaps | Fix in the final pass. It costs little. |
| T7: zero-argument test passes `TOOL_NAME` | Optional. |
| R3: verbatim Gemini script, not the builder in spec trap 2 | Accepted. I confirmed byte identity. Put it in the PR body. |
| R4: older `_` arms | Accepted as out of scope. |
| R2: `ReasoningCleanStop` declares calls | Accepted. The spec §6.3 sentence "an empty list for every other scenario" no longer matches the code. Put this in the PR body, and add the test in Important 2. |

### Recommendations (process, not code)

- **The PR body must state the release effect** (spec §6.6 asks for this). The `docs(core)` commit gives `core` a patch bump and a facade cascade. Commit `86f8b2fe` adds a test in `providers-bedrock/src/stream.rs`. That file is in the packaged crate, and release-plz assigns bumps by file path. So `bedrock` also gets a patch bump, although the commit type is `test`. Say this too.
- **Squash merge can lose the core CHANGELOG wording.** A squash merge folds `docs(core): SMA-567 …` into the PR title. The core CHANGELOG entry then reads as the PR title, not as a "contract clarification" (spec §6.6). Either choose a PR title that reads well as the core entry, or use a rebase merge to keep the `docs(core)` commit.
- Put R2 and R3 in the PR body, because they are differences from the spec text.

### Declined to judge

- `calls_mismatch` with blank-id parallel calls (several names under `""`, arguments joined as `{}{}`). No served subject sends blank ids for the new scenarios, and spec §6.3 does not cover it. Set aside as outside scope.
- The older `_` arms in `fakes::finish`, `declared_finish_reason` and the mock `fixture_finish_reason`. The controller ruled on these in R4.
- The older stale "declines four scenarios" heading in the `openai_responses` module doc (`conformance.rs:3543`). The subject already declined five scenarios before this branch. That is not a regression from this branch.
- Whether the CI gates pass (§9 item 6). A run is in progress, and I did not run builds or tests, as instructed.
- That the Linear issues SMA-858, SMA-859 and SMA-860 exist (§9 item 7). I did not query Linear. The table cites them, and the ledger records that Task 0 filed them.

### Assessment

**Ready to merge?** With fixes.

**Reasoning:** The implementation meets §9 items 1 to 5, and the three fixtures are faithful transcriptions. Fix two items before merge. First, the `floor_violation` doc is now false next to assertion 9, and its Err-count floor hides the more exact `EventAfterError` diagnosis (Important 1, with the `[Err, Err]` test from Minor 1). Second, the R2 `ReasoningCleanStop` branch of the "declares no calls" floor has no negative test (Important 2). The Minor items are stale docs and wrapping, which cost little.
